method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts come from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts, parsed by a bytecode reader, and from scans of the executable named in each fact. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: The call convention of a receiverless call to a Global native, and static Lua call contracts of twelve native registrations: the nine Global natives that waited on that convention (_canCreateActorByName, _getActorByName, _getQuestActorForCutSceneReplay, _isExistStaticActor, _prepareAllCommandStaticActor, _getUTF8StringLength, _getUTF8StringByteLength, _normalizeDisplayName and _replaceMacroCodeString) and the WorldMaster tutorial natives _runCharaSchedulerTutorial, _lookAtPlayerTutorial and _aimCameraTutorial. The convention also settles the call path of _isExistActor, _getStaticActor, _createActor and the Lua helpers that global_u aliases. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish actor names, static actor numbers, command sheet contents, scheduler resources or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.MEASURED: Counted or parsed by the method named in the fact, from the executable or from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/binding_map_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the type registry at 0x00CC9D60, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the world object chain and the invalid-parameter route.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The registrar addresses of the other Global rows are in manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json.

framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.

receiverlessConvention.summary: A receiverless call such as _getStaticActor(24301) is a call of a forwarding closure that the root table __newindex installs. The forwarder looks the name up on the global object and calls it with the global object as the first argument. The trampoline 0x00D04DA0 therefore finds the global object, a table, at Lua stack index 1, and the Lua visible arguments start at index 2 like the arguments of a method call.

rootMetatable.claim: The Lua state creation routine 0x00CD8990 builds a table with one hash slot, stores the C closure 0x00D099B0 in it under the key literal at 0x0110E894, which reads __newindex, and then calls 0x00CF3A90. That wrapper applies 0x00DCE760, which pops the table and stores it as the metatable of the object at the pseudo index 0xFFFFD8EE, the globals table. The table holds no other key, so the globals table has no __index.
A read of a global name is therefore a raw read of the globals table. A script call of _getStaticActor reaches whatever closure the assignment path below stored under that key.

rootAssignment.claim: 0x00D099B0 receives the globals table, the key and the value at stack indexes 1, 2 and 3. It raw reads the globals table under the key through 0x00CF3A50 and tests the result with the function test 0x00CF37C0. When the existing value is a function it pops the read and returns, so a second assignment of a function over a function is dropped.

Otherwise the assignment is intercepted when the new value is a function that is not a C function and the key equals none of four reserved names. The C function test 0x00CF37E0 reads the closure type and the C flag byte at closure +0x06. The reserved names are the strings behind the pointer cells 0x0130D514, 0x0130D518, 0x0130D520 and 0x0130D524, which are __lge_defineWork, __lge_setLoopInterval, _progFunc and _onProgFunc. The string compare is 0x00D07E10.

An intercepted assignment needs the string at engine implementation +0x70 to be nonempty. 0x0078FF82 stores global there through 0x00CC96B0 before any _u script runs. With an empty string, or for any assignment that is not intercepted, the routine stores the pair with the raw set 0x00CF3400 on the globals table at 0x00D09C6E..0x00D09C8A.

The intercepted path resolves the class record named by that string through 0x00CD8870, reads the name of its registered parent through 0x00CC6FA0, raw reads the global of that name and sets the key on the table it finds with the ordinary set operation 0x00CF33C0. The ordinary set runs the class table __newindex 0x00D07EB0, so a key that ends in _inl reaches the descriptor resolver 0x00D07890 with that class table at index 1.

The registered parent of the global object is the Global class record, so the global that 0x00CC6FA0 names is the Global class table. 0x00CD9160 links the parent when 0x00CD99F0 creates the object, and 0x00CC6FA0 returns the pooled name at parent record +0x50.

The routine then strips the suffix _inl from a copy of the key when the key ends with it (0x00712C00 tests the suffix, and 0x00D077B0 then replaces the matched text with the string object at 0x01266B10, which is INFERRED to be the empty string). It pushes the stripped key, pushes a copy of it as the only upvalue of the C closure 0x00D084A0 through 0x00CF32E0 and raw sets the closure on the globals table under the stripped key. A key without the suffix is used unchanged.

The descriptor resolver stores the registered closure under the stripped name in the table at index 1, which is the Global class table here, so the same assignment fills Global._getStaticActor with the native closure and _G._getStaticActor with the forwarder.

forwarder.claim: 0x00D084A0 is the forwarder. It counts the n arguments with 0x00CF34C0, pushes the string at engine implementation +0x70 and raw reads that global, which is the global object. It pushes the upvalue 1, the stripped name, and indexes the global object with it through 0x00CF3440, the get operation that runs metamethods. It pushes a copy of the global object, removes the global object below the function through 0x00CF3510 and pushes copies of the n arguments in order.

It then calls with n + 1 arguments and all results through 0x00CF3DB0 and returns the number of results above its own n arguments. The forwarded call is global[name](global, a1 .. an) and every result of the target is returned.

The key read is a get with metamethods, so the global object is indexed through its own metatable and finds the closure in the Global class table or in its registered parents. The forwarder does not test the result, so a name that resolves to nil makes the call operation fail on a nil value (the run-time result was not observed).

trampoline.claim: Every native closure is 0x00D08000 with the registration record as its light userdata upvalue. It builds the state wrapper through 0x00CF3180 and runs 0x00D04DA0. The trampoline reads the record from upvalue 1 through the upvalue pseudo index 0xFFFFD8ED (0x00CF3530 with 1), loads the engine context through 0x00CF3CE0 and tests that stack index 1 is a table with 0x00CF3740, which compares the type code with 5.

When index 1 is not a table it builds the class and method text through 0x00CCFB20, reports it to the diagnostic object at engine context +0x1CC through 0x00CD4FA0, which calls virtual slot 0x50, and returns zero results. No Lua error is raised on this path.

Otherwise 0x00CD77D0 reads the object behind index 1. It indexes the table by the light userdata key stored at 0x0130D4E0 (0x00010000), takes the userdata and returns the dword in it. 0x00CE1720 accepts the result when the dword at record +0x08 differs from the dword at 0x0130D4F8 (0x00010007). A rejected result is reported through 0x00CD5060, virtual slot 0x54 of the same diagnostic object, and the call returns zero results.

0x00CD77D0 returns zero for a table without that key and the trampoline passes the result to 0x00CE1720 without a null test, which then reads +0x08 of the result. The run-time effect of a table that is not a registered object at index 1 was not observed.

An accepted call runs 0x00D04FE0, which pushes the class and method call frame, and 0x00D19B70, which reads the receiver identity from index 1 and marshals the declared arguments from index 2, as the argument marshalling of the widget contracts records.

globalObject.claim: 0x0078FAD0 calls 0x00CC78A0, which runs 0x00CD99F0, for the pairs global and Global, math and Math, string and String, table and Table, and then 0x00CC72C0 with the flag 1 on the control it returns. 0x00CD99F0 creates the object table through 0x00CD7970 and 0x00CD7690. 0x00CD7690 creates a table with a metatable and a four byte userdata and stores the userdata in the table under the key 0x00010000.

0x00CD99F0 then builds the registration record of the object with 0x00CE2D50, links its registered parent with 0x00CD9160 and finishes with 0x00CE2440. 0x00CC72C0 reaches 0x00CE1DD0, which stores the flag in record +0x7D and clears the byte at +0x7E when the flag is set.

The global object satisfies the table test and the record test of the trampoline. It is a table, and the record behind its key 0x00010000 is the one that 0x00CE2D50 builds. That the userdata holds the record pointer is INFERRED from the shared use of 0x00CD77D0. The same objects serve math:_randomInteger(1, 2) in the shipped scripts, which dispatches through the same trampoline.

The record is not marked as released. 0x00CE1BB0, the test that the instance __index closure 0x00D085B0 runs, answers yes only when the byte at +0x7E is set or when a tentative control has died, and the flag call above leaves the byte clear. The key lookup through the global object therefore reaches the class tables like any other instance.

global_u defines _getTutorialJudge as a function with one parameter whose body is global:_getStaticActor_cpp(320006), a method call on the global object, so the shipped scripts use the same receiver form that the forwarder produces.

corpus.claim: Every shipped call of the eleven Global natives of this record and of _createActor is a free call whose function is read with GETGLOBAL (0 method calls). The argument counts are 1 for _canCreateActorByName (1 site), _getActorByName (4), _getQuestActorForCutSceneReplay (2), _isExistStaticActor (3), _getUTF8StringLength (3), _getUTF8StringByteLength (4), _normalizeDisplayName (1), _isExistActor (7) and _getStaticActor (38), 0 for _prepareAllCommandStaticActor (1) and 3 for _replaceMacroCodeString (1).

consequences.claim: Every Global native, the plain Lua functions that scripts assign to the globals table, and the ten Lua helpers print, tonumber, tostring, type, assert, error, select, unpack, pcall and xpcall that global_u aliases through descriptors with the selector global are called through this forwarder. tostring(x) becomes global.tostring(global, x), which satisfies the receiver table test of the Lua forwarding wrapper 0x00D07F20 -> 0x00D04BF0 that xivl-decomp:docs/script/lua-bootstrap-chunks.md lists as open. The functions of the four reserved names are stored raw and take no receiver, as _onProgFunc records.

A script defined global function is called with the global object as its first parameter, inferred from the same forwarder. No shipped script calls _getTutorialJudge and global_u declares it with one unused parameter, so the parameter count is not evidence of it.

receiverlessOpen: The effect of a forwarded call whose name does not resolve on the global object was not run.
That the userdata under the key 0x00010000 of the global object holds the registration record that 0x00CE2D50 builds is INFERRED, and the record's +0x08 dword was not read.
The text of the two diagnostics 0x00CD4FA0 and 0x00CD5060 emit and the sink behind engine context +0x1CC were not traced.

returns.note: True when the engine name table holds no live entry for the name.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String and asks the engine name table whether the name is known in a loaded state. It pushes false for a known name and true otherwise. It reads no handle and creates nothing. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 with the Utf8String reader 0x0071CE70 and keeps a result byte set to 1. The cell vector size test calls the invalid-parameter route 0x009D22B4 when the vector is empty.

It calls 0x00CC7200 with the engine handle at ExecuteParameters +0x04 and the string. A nonzero answer clears the result byte. 0x00CC7200 jumps to 0x00CD9C60, which looks the name up through 0x00CD8870 with the create flag 0 and returns false for an absent name or the result of 0x00CE16C0, the same three-state test as _isExistActor.
The result byte is pushed through the bool pusher 0x00748870 with the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C. The routine makes no handle lookup and no call to 0x00CD2860.

A name that is present in a state outside the three loaded states also gives true, because only the three-state test is applied. That the native answers whether a script may create an actor under the name is INFERRED from the native name.

rows.callbackKind: thin adapter into a body routine

returns.note: The control behind the name, or Nil.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String. When the engine name table knows the name in a loaded state, the name resolves to a control and the flag byte at +0x7D of the control's object reference is nonzero, it pushes that control. Otherwise it pushes a null control, which the LuaControl* push turns into Nil. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds an empty adapter through 0x0078BB90 and calls the body 0x0078CAF0 with ExecuteParameters, as _isExistActor does.
The body tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as a Utf8String and runs the name test 0x00CC7200. A name that fails it takes the null push.

A known name is looked up again through 0x00CC7A00, which runs 0x00CD8870 with the flag 1 and returns the first dword of the entry, a LuaControl*, or 0. 0x00CC72A0 reads the byte at +0x7D of the object reference of that control through 0x00CD7A30. A zero byte takes the null push.
The success path pushes the control through 0x00748B30. The failure path stores 0 and pushes it through the same pusher. The control pusher pushes Nil for a null control.

0x00CC72A0 reads the byte without a null test of the object reference, so a handle whose reference is null is not guarded here. The entry's first dword is nonzero in the success path because 0x00CC7A00 returned it and the body does not test it before 0x00CC72A0.

returns.note: The control of the static actor.

rows.behavior: Reads one int, turns it into a static actor identity and resolves it. A control that already resolves is pushed at once after the identity's use count is bumped through 0x00CC7160. When none resolves, the callback runs the _getStaticActor body 0x0078CC30, which may create the static actor and suspend the Lua thread until the new control carries the flag at +0x7D.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 with the int reader 0x005819A0 and builds the identity with 0x00CC70E0 on the engine handle, which reaches 0x00D03A50 on the object at engine +0x1C4.
0x00CC7A50 resolves the identity to a control. A nonzero control takes the found path: 0x00CC7160 runs 0x00D037A0 on the identity and the control is pushed through 0x00748B30.

0x00D037A0 returns without a change when the byte at its receiver +0x54 is zero, 0x00D03540 accepts the identity and the byte that 0x00D03340 finds for it equals the byte at 0x0130D426. Otherwise it finds the node of the identity through 0x006D1170 on the container at receiver +0x2C and increments the dword at node +0x0C. The routine returns no value that the callback uses.
The dword that 0x00D037A0 increments is a use count of the static actor identity. The roles of the byte at +0x54 and of 0x0130D426 were not traced.

An identity that does not resolve takes the other path, which builds the empty adapter 0x0078BB90, runs the body 0x0078CC30 and destroys the adapter. The body is the one of _getStaticActor. It resolves the identity again, may call 0x00CC7160 and 0x00CC78C0, pushes a control that has the +0x7D flag and otherwise yields through 0x00CD2860 with a CreateStaticActorResumeChecker built by 0x0078D800.
The body reads cell 0 by the tag byte, so the int cell takes the integer branch through 0x00CC70E0.

resumeChecker.poll: 0x0078D880 resolves the stored identity through 0x00CC7A50 and resumes when 0x00CC72A0 reports the +0x7D flag set.
resumeChecker.note: The same checker as the _getStaticActor row of manifests/boot_native_call_contract.json.

arguments.note: Static actor number or name, the argument list of _getStaticActor.

returns.note: True when the static actor identity is known and resolves to a control.

rows.behavior: Resolves the static actor name or number to an identity exactly like _getStaticActor and pushes true when the identity differs from the empty identity 0xE0000000, the engine knows it and it resolves to a control. It never creates a static actor and never yields.

facts.claim: The callback builds the empty adapter and calls the body 0x0078CE10.

The body tests the cell vector size twice and compares the tag byte at cell +0x0C with 3. Tag 3 reads a Utf8String and calls 0x00CC7130. Any other tag reads an int through 0x005819A0 and calls 0x00CC70E0. Both store the identity dword.

An identity equal to the dword at 0x0130C778 (0xE0000000 in the file image) pushes false. 0x00CC7190 asks whether the engine knows the identity (0x00D035D0 on the object at engine +0x1C4) and a negative answer pushes false. Otherwise 0x00CC7A50 resolves the control and the callback pushes whether it is nonzero.
The result is pushed through 0x00748870. The routine does not read the +0x7D flag and does not call 0x00CC7160, 0x00CC78C0 or 0x00CD2860.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and returns nothing. For each static actor number in the global list at 0x0134B77C..0x0134B780 it builds the identity and, when no control with the +0x7D flag exists for it, hands the identity to the request routine 0x00767100. It creates no control itself and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The return and argument lists are both the empty list builder 0x0072B440. The callback reads no cell.

The callback resolves the world chain through 0x00CC7510 (X = [R], Y = [X +0x04]) and keeps the object at Y +0xD8. It walks the dword vector whose begin and end pointers are at 0x0134B77C and 0x0134B780 and calls the invalid-parameter route when the begin pointer is above the end pointer or the cursor leaves the vector.

For each element it builds the identity with 0x00CC70E0 and resolves it with 0x00CC7A50. A nonzero control goes to the flag test. For a zero control 0x00CC7180 decides. A true answer goes straight to the request call. A false answer calls 0x00CC7160 and resolves again through 0x00CC78C0, where a zero result goes to the request call and a nonzero result goes to the flag test.

At the request call, reached as above or when 0x00CC72A0 reads a zero +0x7D byte, the callback calls 0x00767100 on the object at Y +0xD8 with the identity address. That routine adds 0x20 to its receiver and forwards the identity to 0x00582BC0. The effect of 0x00582BC0 was not traced.

The vector at 0x0134B77C is filled while the sheet named by the literal at 0x00FD8610, which reads command, loads. The loop reads each id of the sheet row ranges, keeps the ids 0x2EE0..0x32C7, 0x5208..0x55EF, 0x5DC0..0x61A7, 0x6590..0x6783, 0x7530 and 0x7595 whose byte at column 3 is zero and appends them through 0x00723C60. 0x00785F90 then rebuilds the vector with a copy and a swap.

The ids are command numbers of the command sheet and the static actors are the command actors of the native name. The meaning of the byte at column 3 and of the sheet object returned by the virtual call at 0x0076AC04 was not traced.

rows.callbackKind: thin adapter into a body routine
rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String and pushes its length in UTF-8 characters, counting one per lead byte. The count comes from 0x00445E50, which caches it in the string object. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the empty adapter and calls the body 0x0078CF80.
The body tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70, calls 0x00445E50 on the string and pushes the result as an int through 0x00584F70.

0x00445E50 returns the cached count when the flag byte at string +0x10 is set. Otherwise it walks the buffer at string +0x00. A null buffer gives 0. Each step adds 1 and advances by 1 byte for a byte below 0x80, 2 for 0xC0..0xDF, 3 for 0xE0..0xEF, 4 for 0xF0..0xF7, 5 for 0xF8..0xFB and 6 for 0xFC..0xFD. A byte 0x80..0xBF, 0xFE or 0xFF advances by 0. It stores the count at +0x0C and sets the flag.

A scan position on a byte with step 0 does not advance, so the loop at 0x00445E70 has no exit for it. A well formed UTF-8 string never lands there. The run-time effect on malformed text was not observed.

returns.note: The byte count without the terminator.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String and pushes the size dword of the string object minus 1. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the empty adapter and calls the body 0x0078CFE0.
The body reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70, calls 0x004451F0, which returns the dword at string +0x08 minus 1, and pushes the result as an int through 0x00584F70.
The dword at +0x08 counts the terminating zero byte, so the result is the byte length. That the dword is a size with the terminator is INFERRED from the subtraction.

returns.note: The name unchanged, or lowercased with a capital letter at the start of each word.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String. A name that contains a byte below 0x20 or ends with the text of the literal at 0x00FD48B0 (a space and three exclamation marks) is pushed unchanged. Any other name is converted in place, first to lowercase with 0x00445EE0 and then with 0x00445220, which raises the first letter of each word, and the converted text is pushed. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 and tests the string with 0x00445450, which answers true as soon as it meets a byte below 0x20 before the terminator. A true answer jumps to the push of the unchanged string.

Otherwise the callback builds a string from the literal at 0x00FD48B0 and compares the tail of the name with it: a shorter name gives false, an equal length compares both strings with 0x00445D20 and a longer name compares the tail through 0x00448030. A match jumps to the push of the unchanged string. The counts that this compare passes are the 0x00445E50 character counts.

A name that fails both tests is converted. The callback pushes the flags 1, 1, 0, 0 and 0, calls 0x00445EE0 on the string and 0x00445220 on its result, then pushes the same string object through the Utf8String pusher 0x007487C0.
0x00445EE0 walks the string by UTF-8 sequence length and adds 0x20 to each byte 0x41..0x5A. It also rewrites a second byte of some two-byte sequences that start with 0xC3 or 0xC5.

0x00445220, with the first flag set, acts only at the first byte and at each byte that follows a 0x20 byte. It subtracts 0x20 from a byte 0x61..0x7A there. It also maps two-byte sequences that start with 0xC3 or 0xC5 to their uppercase forms, and with the fourth and fifth flags zero it uses no exception list.

The native title cases a display name unless it carries a control byte or the three exclamation mark suffix, which then marks a name to keep as typed. The role of the suffix is INFERRED from the literal.
The conversion changes the argument cell's string in place before the push. The push copies the text, so the Lua string argument is not touched.

arguments.note: The replacement. A cell of tag 6 skips the replacement.

returns.note: The text with every pattern occurrence replaced.

rows.behavior: Reads a text, a pattern and a replacement. A tag 6 replacement cell pushes the text unchanged. A replacement without a byte below 0x20 replaces every occurrence of the pattern with 0x0067AC00. A replacement with such a byte replaces the occurrences that lie outside the spans between the bytes 0x02 and 0x03 of the text. It pushes the result and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x0073D770 appends three entries, each from registry entry 3, the Utf8String operator.

The callback copies cell 0 into a local string through 0x00447200, reads cell 1 and tests the byte at cell 2 +0x0C against 6 after a size test of 3 cells. A tag 6 jumps to the push of the local string. Otherwise it reads cell 2 through 0x0071CE70.

0x00445450 tests the replacement for a byte below 0x20. When it finds none, the callback calls 0x0067AC00 with the local text, the pattern and the replacement. That routine searches the pattern from offset 0 through 0x004465A0, replaces each hit through 0x00447EA0, searches again after the hit and returns the replacement count, which the callback ignores.

A replacement with a control byte takes the loop at 0x006FF73C..0x006FFA3F. It copies the text, the pattern and the replacement into local strings and reads the bytes at 0x012C3116 (0x02) and 0x012C3115 (0x03) from the data section image as the start and end bytes of a macro span. It finds the pattern with 0x006BE5E0 from a cursor. When the hit lies before the next macro start, or no macro follows, it replaces the hit through 0x00596E10 and moves the cursor and the span positions by the length difference. When the hit lies inside a span it moves the cursor behind the span end.

Both initial span positions are the first 0x02 byte of the text, because both initial searches use the byte at 0x012C3116, so the first span has zero width and a hit inside it is replaced. Later spans are found by searching for a 0x02 behind the previous hit and for the 0x03 behind that. The loop was not run on text with several spans.
The local text is assigned back to the copy of cell 0 and pushed through 0x007487C0 at 0x006FFA6C. The argument cells keep their values.

The bytes 0x02 and 0x03 delimit inline macro codes of the client text format, and the native keeps the macro codes of a text intact while it substitutes a plain phrase. This is INFERRED from the names and the byte values.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order of the framework.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.
The Lua bytecode facts come from the installed client scripts. Their sources are not redistributed, and the tracked script metadata holds names and line numbers only.

The convention describes the closures the root table assignment installs. It does not establish the contents of the engine name tables or the record behind the global object, which were not read at run time.

The callbacks that dereference a resolved identity or a lookup result without a test, namely the tutorial natives for a chara that is not found and the control query of the trampoline for a table that is not a registered object, were not run with an absent value, so their run-time effect is unknown.
The invalid-parameter route ends in a process terminate on the evidence of the target cursor contract. The calls that reach it with an empty cell vector were not run.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish command numbers, actor names, scheduler resources, camera behavior or server behavior.
